newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares continue rise to close just off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares continue rise to close just off peaks.

text.p: Italian stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday just below new record highs set on the all-share and blue chip indices during a session of active trading, but slightly lower volume than on Tuesday.
The Mibtel index ended 1.15 percent up at 13,469 after a new high at 13,541 while the Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.16 percent higher at 20,485 after a 20,631 peak.
"The latest surge was made on buying of telecoms and energy group ENI. If market interest were now to turn to banks and insurances we could see a further rise," one dealer said.
ENI, on the third day of its third tranche share offer, put on 1.13 percent to 9,610 lire.
Sentiment was boosted by new highs seen in Btp futures in a market where optimism reigns over the single European currency and the possibility of an Italian interest rate cut.
In telecoms, Telecom Italia closed 2.62 percent up at 5,670, mobile phone operator TIM rose 1.83 percent to 5,785 and Stet holding gained 2.5 percent to 10,215 lire.

Losers against the trend included Fiat seen to have "reached its target", off 0.31 percent to 6,180 lire, food group Parmalat slipped 2.14 percent to 2,465, while clothing and textile groups Marzotto and Stefanel lost 1.46 percent and 1.65 percent respectively.

In banks, Credito Italiano continued to stand out, ending 1.85 percent higher at 3,198 lire, even if volume was below that of previous days, dealers said. Ambroveneto was also firmer, up 3.67 percent at 4,694.
The FIB30 stock index futures ended higher again with the September contract at a late 20,770 after a session high at 20,915 on stop-loss buying. Dealers noted good foreign buying.
Overall traded volume was estimated down on the previous session's 1.75 trillion lire at around 1.45 trillion lire.
